newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble steady as funds sought for T-bill buying.
newsitem.headline: Rouble steady as funds sought for T-bill buying.

text.p: The rouble was stable in lively trading on Monday and dealers said its usual slow decline had stopped because banks sought funds to invest in the government bond market after yields rose there.
T-bill prices came under further pressure on Monday on news President Boris Yeltsin's planned bypass operation may be postponed or cancelled.
But the Yeltsin news did not affect the rouble.
"Treasury bill prices have fallen recently and banks seem to be using roubles to buy them as it is more profitable than investing in dollars," an Aljba Alliance Bank dealer said.
Another dealer said higher rouble demand could also reflect active bidding by a major bank.
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,389-92 per dollar compared with an early 5,387-90 and 5,397-5,400 late on Friday. Tomorrow roubles were steady at 5,395-99 per dollar.
The central bank said it had set 5,369/5,409 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Monday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 50-70 percent compared with Friday's late 10-30 percent.

Dealers said the relatively thin rouble/dollar market, which is strictly controlled by the central bank, was as usual unaffected by political news and did not react to the news on Yeltsin's heart surgery.
The doctor tipped to carry out the planned operation on Yeltsin said on Sunday that the country's leader could wait another 1-1/2 to two months and might have to resign himself to not having it.
